name: Muse Spark Open 816B-A42B
purpose: Open-weights 816B total / 42B active natively multimodal model built for coding and agentic work (card): multi-step reasoning, end-to-end agentic task completion, coding agents, tool use, multimodal reasoning, synthetic data generation and LLM-as-a-judge. The open version has additional safety post-training for use without system guardrails.

license.name: Muse Model License (Muse Spark Open version)
license.notes: LICENSE.md read (copy in the unsloth mirror repo; the card links the Meta repo file, which is gated and was not compared): MIT-style grant (use, copy, modify including fine-tune, distill, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, sell). Conditions: keep copyright, license and the Usage Policy (Exhibit A, prohibited uses, not for under-18s); display 'Built with Muse Spark Open' in each product or service using the model or derivatives (derivatives include any model trained or distilled from its outputs); Model-as-a-Service providers with aggregate gross revenue above US$20 million must notify Meta and sign a separate agreement; Meta claims no ownership of outputs.

architecture.kind: multimodal Mixture-of-Experts transformer with gated attention, plus a 1.8B Perception Encoder (50 layers, 4096 output dim) and an audio encoder
architecture.gguf_arch: muse_spark (config model_type; llama.cpp support listed on the card)
architecture.attention: GQA 128 query / 16 KV heads, head dim 64, gated attention with QK-norm; config layer_types alternate sliding_attention and full_attention (every 4th layer full in the first entries read)
architecture.drafter: nvidia/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-DFlash2: NVIDIA's DFlash 2 speculative-decoding draft model (4.38B dense parameters, 5 decoder layers with non-causal sliding-window attention, window 2048, block size 8; token embedding and output head shared with the target). It drafts a block of candidate tokens in one non-causal forward pass and a pairwise path selector walks one coherent path through each position's top-k candidates; the target verifies. Trained on prompts from Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v2 with responses generated by the target model, evaluated for acceptance length on SPEED-Bench and MT-Bench (card; no acceptance-length numbers given in the part read), tested on NVIDIA Blackwell GB300; NVIDIA Open Model Agreement license plus Meta's Muse license. Other DFlash2 drafters exist (RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2, Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark), not read.

strengths: Top agentic scores in the vendor table (MCP-Atlas 89.2, JobBench 61.8, ZeroBench 50.0) and 1M context
Natively multimodal input: text, image, video, audio
License allows commercial use and distillation with an attribution line
weaknesses: Behind Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 on coding agents (Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSWE) in the vendor's own table
Needs 700 GB of VRAM at NVFP4 by the card; 'Built with' attribution and the Usage Policy follow every derivative
soft.behavior: Reasoning effort low/medium/high/xhigh (default xhigh); recommended temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, top_k disabled; the card advises high or xhigh for coding and agentic tasks. Very short or low-resolution videos may be refused as not viewable.
soft.maturity: Released 2026-10-15 by Meta; over 40 community quantizations within weeks.

tona_fit.reason: Beyond every hardware class: 816B total parameters, 1644 GB in BF16 and 175.64 GB even at the smallest GGUF quant (UD-IQ1_S), against a budget of about 52 GB (largest Mac class) to 80 GB (32 GB PC with 64 GB RAM). The license is permissive and the agentic scores are strong, so the model matters as a yardstick and for MoE research, not as something to offer. Its DFlash 2 drafter (block-diffusion speculative decoding) is the transferable part.
blockers: no hardware class can hold it
no Tona backend for the Muse Spark architecture
